Key Activities: Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.
Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work.
Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.
Identifies and researches trends and developments in mass data processing concepts, methods and techniques.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems.
Manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.
Defines processing and production specifications and guidelines for the contracting of development work to internal service areas, outside agencies and contractors.
Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data.
Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements and determines objectives and priorities. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify developmental projects and operational systems and processes or program results. When findings are challenged or misinterpreted, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in mass data processing.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design and of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management including the management of human and financial resources.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of production and dissemination activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on program results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations and identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the production and dissemination methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements.
